steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The sound I heard when I was passed out...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It was you, sharpening your sword.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: It got some dirt on it on the way back.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It had better be sharp enough.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: My neck is sturdier than you might think.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: That's not for you to decide.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hah... Are we on top of a spire?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: I'm not going to let you jump off, if that's what you mean. As I said, there are no second chances.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It almost sounds like you want me to live.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: It doesn't matter what I want. It's my responsibility.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: You also have own responsibilities, don't you? You returned to Leithanien. Don't run away again, like a child.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Perhaps your employer forgot to mention this, but Graf Urtica is dead.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: But the Urtica Grafschaft still exists.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: You're still the last of House Urtica.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But I never wanted—

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Running away doesn't make problems disappear.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: No one can choose their birth. In that sense, we're all the same.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is that what you tell yourself to justify serving as an executioner for that evil old fart? That you had no choice but to become his follower?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Nein. It's how I remind myself what it took to gain the freedom I have now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Using the name Urtica, the one you call an 'evil old fart' changed my family's destiny.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Everything I do today, I do to protect the hard-earned freedom of myself and many like me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're... thanking the Witch King?!

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: I'm just stating a fact.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A 'fact,' huh?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What about the 'fact' that he spilled so much blood? What about the 'fact' that his remnants have claimed so many innocent victims?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Did you think you could ignore all the pain he inflicted on others, just because of some convenient 'fact'?!

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: The Witch King is dead. Let the historians, politicians, and everyone else with too much time on their hands judge his deeds.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: I'm a warrior. My only concern is the battle in front of me, and the battle to come.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: If he truly left anything behind, then whether his legacy is good or bad isn't up to him anymore. It's up to those who make use of it.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: As his heir, that's how you should be thinking.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't you dare look at me like that!

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Your wounds are going to open up.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't need sympathy from a remnant of the Witch King!

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Graf—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Not another word!

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Ebenholz.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Which of us do you really think isn't brave enough to face the 'facts' of the Witch King?
That'll do, Lessing.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: ...Welcome back.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Are the Arts ready?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Arts...?

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Hopefully what's in your head will come in useful, lamb of Urtica.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Now, let me see it—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: The melody is surprisingly intact, considering Leithanians know nothing of souls.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Sometimes I wonder if these people meticulously recorded even what Herkunftshorn mumbled in his sleep...

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: I almost miss those metaphors of his, when he used to curse out his tutor.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Y-You knew the old fart? Who are you?

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Old fart? Is that how you talk about the elders of your own family? I thought you Leithanians were all about etiquette and manners. Well, that's the one thing you have in common with him, I suppose.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I have NOTHING in common with him!

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Stop screaming. Are you a three-month old baby? Crying any louder won't make anyone listen.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Why don't you do something useful with your mouth? I could teach you some vocal Arts that can be cast with your tongue alone.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm not taking lessons from a minion of the Witch King!

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: A ball of Arts? Was that what hit you the last time, Lessing?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I was careless.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: How many times do I have to tell you: You need to do more than swing your sword around! Train your Arts perception! I hope you never tell anyone I raised you, you stupid sheep!

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I never have.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: As for you, I suppose it's noteworthy that you can manage that without an Arts unit.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: But your manipulation of energy couldn't be more clumsy. Are you trying to blow yourself up? Who taught you to use your lesions like that? The imbeciles in the spires?

spans.text: But your manipulation of energy couldn't be more clumsy. Are you
to blow yourself up? Who taught you to use your lesions like that? The imbeciles in the spires?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's all the Witch King's—

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Fools. They learned from Herkunftshorn's madness, but without a sliver of his skill.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Mmph—Argh!

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: That's better, my little lamb. It's best that you stay put, for everyone's safety.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Check the defensive enchantment, Lessing.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Professor Hoffmann is on his way. You should wait until he arrives.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: We need to get this over with quickly, before we draw the attention of the Empresses' Voice and the Gesatzswächter.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Fine. Gerhard won't be of much help, but it's not the worst thing for him to learn a lesson or two.

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: The Genesis Horn...

steps.name: Cranky Old Man
steps.text: Hmph. How long as it been?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Karl Schmidt Street.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: That place again? It's just an old street where a bunch of failed artists make their homes. I've already investigated it more than a few times.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin received a phone call before his death.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It was from an old baron by the name of Lukas, who lives on Karl Schmidt Street. Apparently, he's called for the Gendarmerie many times because of noise in the streets.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: The old nobles are all like that, overreacting to the smallest things. They think they can order the people down here around like servants, even though they've been kicked out of their spires.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: What I mean is, I wouldn't take it too seriously.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin's actions indicate the likelihood of a plausible lead there.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: ...Were you even listening? Just because he went there doesn't mean he thought it was worth investigating.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: He may have been the commander of the Gendarmerie, but he was just a Vizegraf, and a houseless outsider at that.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Twenty-year-old honor made him little more than a glorified servant for the great nobles of a place like Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: He answered the Baron's call, not because it was a useful lead, but because he had to.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This information has little relevance to the objective.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Hey, don't just go! At least—wait up!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: That shop.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: 'Frau Schultz's Fine Hats'? I don't usually wear hats because of my halo.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Just go in.
Good afternoon.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Good afternoon, meine Dame.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Oh... By your appearance, I take it you're a local?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: You could say that.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Do you know how I can get to Karl Schmidt Street?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'm new around here. I don't suppose young nobles like yourself leave their spires very often. I'll ask someone else.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: No need. Just follow this street until the fourth statue, then make a left. You'll see it in the distance.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: See what in the distance?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: You didn't know? Karl Schmidt Street is also known as Marigold Alley.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Marigold...

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: It's where the great composer Karl Schmidt once lived.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: He wrote some famous pieces about marigolds under the sun, making the alley a kind of holy ground for art lovers.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Interesting. I've never read about that.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: A little anecdote, the kind you hear all over Zwillingstürme. Hardly even a story.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Well, danke. For the directions and the story.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Incidentally, you're not old enough to be buying a graduation cap, are you?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Oh, I'm waiting for someone.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: If we happen to be heading to the same place... would you like to come with me?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: ...Thank you for the offer.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: But the music of the Kaiserinnen will guide me.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: May the melody of Zwillingstürme be ever long and winding, like the rivers and the clouds.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: ...You can come out now.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Explain your actions.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: That was an Empresses' Voice who just passed by.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: She seemed decent enough, but unfortunately we're not walking the same path.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You're a little later than we agreed on, Viviana.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I met... a remarkable young man on the streets.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Now I'm sure we're not the only ones looking into this case.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You sound a little sad about that.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja. The spy was practically a child.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You stopped. What's the matter?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm listening.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The music of the Kaiserinnen is still playing.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Zwillingstürme still bathes in their wonderful melody.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But... can a melody played by divergent wills remain in harmony forever?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You fear the Empresses' Voice. Is your employer an enemy of the Empresses?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Are you out of your mind? Don't ask that question out on the street!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We'll be entering the alley soon. I will ask then.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Fine. You want to know if I'm in league with the people who killed Loris Bordin? Absolutely not.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: I'm a Lupo, which I would hope is obvious. I was born near Siracusa.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: In the early years of the Witch King's reign, not long after Siracusa broke away from Leithanien, how do you think he and his followers treated my people?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I was inquiring about you personally, not the history of your family.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Is there a difference?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I had assumed that you made your own choices of your own free will.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Free will? Not in my family. I was born to carry our destiny.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Just like the lady who recently became an Empresses' Voice. She went from Leithanien to Kazimierz, and from Kazimierz back to Leithanien. Was any of that her own choice?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am inferring that it's complicated. This will make it difficult to discern friend from foe.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Hah... Why do you think they call Laterano Paradise?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Stop.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: What's the matter? Karl Schmidt Street is just ahead. The Empresses' Voice went there. Maybe Bordin really did find something.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The alley has changed from before.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is too quiet.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Are these pieces all by Frau Seemann?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Ja, meine Dame.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: All drafts of Der Tod des Hexenkönigs.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: I didn't dare touch them, nor did I understand them, so I left them where they were.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: What about anything else from the past few years?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: The past few years... There's not much to show. She often said that her passion ended that autumn, twenty-three years ago. Would you like to peruse her earlier works?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: If you don't mind.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Seemann's early works are characterized by refined touches and bright, lively colors.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Frieda Seemann wanted to capture authentic emotions with her brush. She had an excellent memory, and made good use of Originium Arts to recreate snapshots in time.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: She was still young when I saw her in the Witch King's Spire for the first time.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: She had an almost Minoan liveliness to her, less of the stiffness of your average Leithanian noblewoman.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Her easy-going nature attracted people from all walks of life.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Frieda's friends used to hold poetry gatherings here in this alley... Your parents were among them.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My parents? They came here too?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Did they never tell you? This is where they met.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Your father wasn't a Kurfürst-in-waiting quite yet. He came from Sturmland to Einwald, and often participated in gatherings of young people in Marigold Alley.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: One day, a young woman of common stock mustered the courage to read a little poem she wrote at Frau Seemann's poetry gathering.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And that was my mother?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: She never told me any of this.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Her brow's always been furrowed, for as far back as I can remember...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Lucinda Droste was a shy, gentle girl with soft, gleaming eyes. Gazing upon her was like sitting by the lakeside in summer, with a gentle breeze brushing by.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Werner fell in love at first sight, almost missing His Majesty's summons.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: If Brandt hadn't covered for him, he would have been part of a statue in front of the Spire by the time House Hochberg's soldiers arrived at Einwald.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: This was still during the reign of the Witch King?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Hard to believe, isn't it?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: But that era was resplendent in its own way, much like the painting before you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A resplendent... marigold.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: This painting looks familiar. I think I've seen it before.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But where?

a.text: 'Viviana.'
'I'm sorry, but I need to take this painting away.'
'Your mother is gone. I'll have someone clear out the room.'
'I couldn't possibly leave you here with no one to take care of you.'
'Someone will be here to take you away soon.'
'Don't cry. You'll meet new friends out there. There will be people who love you, even without Mutti and Vati.'
'You'll see the marigolds with your own eyes.'
'See for me if they're blooming, like in the painting.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...A flower chasing the sun.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The clouds above Sturmland rarely clear up. It was cold and wet up in the spire. Father tried many things, and hired many casters, but could never get them to survive in the flower pots.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But here in this tiny Zwillingstürme alley, they're everywhere.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's... warm.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Where are you going, Viviana?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...An enemy?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Viviana!
The music is faint, almost imperceptible.
It seems distant, but also nearby.
It transcends time, transcends memories, linking them in the same space.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You're going back.

a.text: Ernst's condition deteriorated rapidly. Even the best healers the Twins could find couldn't save his life.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Which means you could be the new Kurfürst of Sturmland.

a.text: When I first came here, I thought I was going to be a poet.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: What about Lucinda?

a.text: I certainly hope she'll come with me, but I won't force her. She's talented. She could become a great painter under Frau Seemann's tutelage.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You love her, and she loves you.

a.text: Which is why I can't lie to her.
I'm no longer the carefree youngest son of the Hochbergs. From this day forth, my life belongs to Sturmland and to House Hochberg. Not to myself.
The nobles will have a whole gaggle of young ladies lined up, all vying to be my wife.
I wouldn't be able to promise her anything, even if she were willing to come. If we lose the power struggle, she could end her days as a handmaiden in our spire.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: His Majesty... the Witch King is dead. The Spire that towered over Leithanien has fallen. Our days of being slaves to fate were expected to be left in the past.

a.text: At the very least, we now know that the name of our fate isn't 'the Witch King.'

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Just give it one last try, won't you? Either take her with you, or stay here for her.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Just like the night when the Witch King fell, I pray that the kind and gentle will have their happy ending.
The music grows clearer.
Unlike the performance of the statues, this music is alive.
Like a kindly hand, it pulls her forward, down the stairs, away from the wind and rain.
It is close. Almost there. Down the stairs, and the sunlight is waiting outside—

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The car is here.

a.text: Lucinda is not here.
I must find her.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Everyone is waiting for you.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Witch King is dead. Your men must return to their lands, in accordance with our agreement with the Twins.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You must leave the city before noon. The armies of the other Kurfürsten are watching your every move.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Sturmland... Nein, the fate of Leithanien falls on your shoulders.

a.text: When did you become such a stranger, Brandt?
You always wear that helmet. I can't see your eyes. Sometimes, I can't even tell if it's you speaking, or another Gesatzswächter.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Because it makes no difference whether it's me or another Gesatzswächter.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Leithanien cannot afford another civil war. Sturmland needs a Kurfürst who the people will get behind.

a.text: You're not here to protect me, are you?
Just like you didn't protect Ernst or father that night.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...Do you remember, Werner? When I was selected for Gesatzswächter training, I came to you and Ernst and told you I wanted to stay.

a.text: You grew up with us and swore fealty to House Hochberg. You didn't want to go back on your vow.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: But you told me—

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: 'You're defending something far more important than any person's life, more important than House Hochberg.'

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I never forgot that. Not even for a moment.

a.text: Alright then.
Is fate truly so impossible to resist, Brandt?

steps.text: No, don't go.
Don't give up hope.
At least, not so easily...
The young Kurfürst turns around and leaves, but Viviana does not want to follow. She tries her hardest to go back.
A golden glow always fills the alley in autumn. Her mother must be somewhere in there, simply unable to make it in time.
She runs, she searches.
Marigolds bloom under the sun, just like the hopes her parents once had for the future.
She wants to grab ahold of her mother, to grab ahold of her father's silhouette from the memory.
As though she could change something if she did.
Change the tragedy that was her father's life... and change her own.
Year after year, the golden flowers take in the city's joy, anger, and sorrow, remaining as bright as ever in bloom.
But some blooming hopes were left behind forever, twenty-three years ago.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why couldn't I grab it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Is fate truly so impossible to resist?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Viviana! Around you!
Viviana looks up in a trance.
The music stops.
The melody seems to freeze in place, then becomes rushing energy.
Like dark clouds, the Arts tear the sunlight apart and rush toward her.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ugh—!

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: No need to fear, I'm here with you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A cello...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Mental Arts.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The music is awakening our memories of Werner.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mother... Father...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Over here, Viviana. I'll cover your ears with my hands.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: They're... gone...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I couldn't change anything...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Don't listen to it. Whatever you're seeing in your imagination isn't happening in the present.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The remnants of the Witch King are in this alley. They knew we were coming.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ugh... there are too many of them.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I can't deal with them all. We need to escape—
Another sound emerges.
It is like a melody, but cannot be sung. It is like a bell, but continuous, without pausing.
It is a declaration that rings in the chambers of the heart.
Like the brightest setting sun, radiant purple Arts shine through the clouds and fill the streets.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: This melody... the Gesatzswächter?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Brandt? Is that you?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...Take Werner's daughter inside.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: As for you, embers of evil...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Filthy dregs picked from the trash heap—

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: —How dare you defile Zwillingstürme!
